Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of two line segments, an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(-4,0)$  with radius $3$, and an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(1,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of ${\int }_{-7}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $4$ parts: the arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-7,-1]$, the line segment for $x\in [-1,1]$, the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [1,3]$, and the line segment for $x\in [3,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-7}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-7}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-7,-1].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-7}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-\frac{9\pi }{2}.
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot 4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-2.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-7}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =-\frac{9\pi }{2}+2+\pi -2 \\  & =-\frac{7\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
